subject: Genetics
title: What Makes a Genetic Disease
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What Makes a Genetic Disease.

hook.text: About 6,000 diseases trace to a single misspelling in DNA. One wrong letter can wreck an entire protein.

buildup.text: Genes encode proteins. A mutation can make the protein fold wrong, work poorly, or vanish entirely.

discovery.text: Some genetic diseases need only one bad copy. Others need two. Inheritance pattern determines who gets sick.

twist.text: Not all mutations cause disease. Many are neutral. A few are even beneficial. Context decides the outcome.

climax.text: Genetic diseases reveal how precisely our code must run. One error in three billion letters can change a life.

punchline.text: One letter wrong. One protein broken. One life changed.

quiz.question: How many known diseases trace to a single gene error?
